stem: A nurse provides preconception health teaching to women capable of becoming pregnant. Which folic-acid recommendation is appropriate for the general population?

options.A: Get 400 micrograms of folic acid every day
options.B: Use folic acid only when actively trying to conceive
options.C: Wait until pregnancy is confirmed before starting folic acid
options.D: Use folic acid only when there is a family history of neural tube defects

rationale: CDC recommends that all women capable of becoming pregnant get 400 micrograms of folic acid every day. Daily folic acid helps prevent neural tube defects and should not be delayed until pregnancy is confirmed or limited only to people with a family history. A is correct for the general population; individuals with special risk factors may require individualized clinician guidance.
educational_objective: Teach the CDC's routine daily folic-acid recommendation for women capable of becoming pregnant.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Folic Acid: Sources and Recommended Intake
source_locator: Overview — CDC recommends all women capable of becoming pregnant get 400 mcg folic acid daily; Supplements — daily vitamin with 400 mcg
source_claim_supported: CDC recommends 400 mcg of folic acid every day for all women capable of becoming pregnant to help prevent neural tube defects.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preconception care, pregnancy-related health promotion, and preventive teaching
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — folic acid and neural-tube-defect prevention

source_original.stem: A nurse is providing health promotion education to a group of women of childbearing age, regardless of current pregnancy status or plans. The nurse should recommend:

options.A: Adequate folic acid for all women, since defects occur early
options.B: Folic acid being unnecessary unless actively trying to conceive
options.C: Folic acid supplementation only after pregnancy is confirmed
options.D: Folic acid only for women with a family history of defects

source_original.rationale: Because neural tube development occurs very early in pregnancy (often before a woman even realizes she is pregnant), the CDC and other health organizations recommend that all women of childbearing age who could become pregnant consume adequate folic acid, rather than waiting until pregnancy is confirmed, to help reduce the risk of neural tube defects.
source_original.source_detail: CDC folic-acid recommendation: all women capable of becoming pregnant should get 400 mcg folic acid daily to help prevent neural tube defects. CDC page current 2026-06-02; reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Replaced vague 'adequate folic acid' wording with CDC's exact 400 mcg daily recommendation and explicitly scoped the item to the general population so higher-risk individualized regimens do not create a second answer.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC folic-acid guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: CDC page dated June 2, 2026 and checked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: CDC directly states all women capable of becoming pregnant should get 400 mcg folic acid daily and links this intake to NTD prevention.

distractor_audit.B: CDC recommendation is not limited to active conception attempts.
distractor_audit.C: Waiting for pregnancy confirmation is inconsistent with routine preconception prevention guidance.
distractor_audit.D: Routine recommendation applies regardless of family-history status.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: General-population wording prevents confusion with higher-dose regimens for selected high-risk patients.
audit_findings.cueing: Short parallel alternatives; exact dose is clinically necessary rather than a superficial cue.
audit_findings.blueprint: Preconception preventive teaching fits Health Promotion and Maintenance.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked CDC lines 36 and 58; A remains uniquely correct.
